study.title: Deep Learning Models for Automatic Classification of Anatomic Location in Abdominopelvic Digital Subtraction Angiography
study.venue: Journal of Imaging Informatics in Medicine

imaging.modality_detail: Routine abdominopelvic DSA sequences; unsubtracted sequences excluded; 16-bit 1024x1024 DICOM resized to 256x256 8-bit JPEG
imaging.territory_detail: Abdominal aorta, celiac trunk, SMA, IMA, right and left external iliac arteries
imaging.frames_per_sequence: Sequences capped at 50 images; 21,129 images in 819 sequences

data_released.detail: Deidentified DSA images and labels available from the corresponding author by request

annotation.annotator_expertise: Interventional radiology attending physicians with 4 and 5 years of post-fellowship experience
annotation.inter_rater_value: Cohen's kappa 0.989 for location class; 0.629 for initial and final key images

task.task_description: Six-class sequence-level classification of anatomic location (aorta, celiac, SMA, IMA, right/left EIA) in abdominopelvic DSA using Mode models aggregating per-image ResNet50 predictions (trained on full or key-image data) and an attention-based MIL model that also identifies key images.
task.clinical_application: Automated anatomic localization in DSA as an initial step toward automated interpretation, report generation, coding and billing

architecture_names: MIL model (ResNet50 + transformer encoder + attention MLP)

temporal_evidence.quote: A transformer encoder is attached to the end of that backbone after average pooling to account for dependencies in features identified in individual images within a sequence.

method.class_imbalance_handling: Supplemented IMA class with 46 additional procedures; split chosen for most even class balance via search of 9e6 permutations
method.explainability_method: MIL attention weights identifying top-5 contributing images compared with manual key images

G1.quote: Data used for the model development and evaluation were relatively small, constrained by the time required for manual labeling.

G2.quote: The data are acquired from a single institution with imaging equipment from a single vendor.

G3.quote: The temporal relationship between images within the sequence is not captured in this architecture

G5.quote: This cost may stand as a substantial barrier to scalability of a manual “key” frame identification approach to larger and more diverse datasets.

G6.quote: The retrospective nature of the data acquisition may produce bias with respect to the spectrum of vascular anatomy and pathology.

G7.quote: provide a weighted score of the contribution of each individual image to the classification based on an attention mechanism

G9.quote: a larger and more balanced dataset could potentially enhance training and testing results

other_limitations: Post-surgical vascular anatomy (e.g., transplant anastomoses) excluded
Label set limited to major first-order abdominopelvic arteries, excluding many DSA sequences
Manual key-frame approach limited to retrospective analyses
future_work: Expand classification to additional first and second order vascular structures
Automated assistance of report generation, coding and billing
Component of a fully automated DSA interpretation system and physician decision support
